 This month, Brad Pitt will reprise his Oscar-winning role as Cliff Booth from Once Upon a Time in Hollywood in a new spin-off movie, The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth . Unlike the original, which was written and directed by Quentin Tarantino , the spin-off has been helmed by Pitt's regular collaborator David Fincher , with Tarantino performing only writing duties. It's a massive project, with Netflix having reportedly spent $200 million on it. Before The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth begins its IMAX-exclusive run later this month, Pitt's latest film will make its debut on the PVOD market.

 The movie in question served as a follow-up to Pitt's highest-grossing hit as a leading man, F1 , which was released last year. The sports drama, directed by Joseph Kosinski , grossed more than $630 million worldwide against a budget reported to be as high as $300 million. Pitt quickly began work on The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth , but his immediate follow-up to F1 was a far riskier bet.
 The film reunited him with his Fury director David Ayer , who was on a hot streak at the time with two Jason Statham vehicles — The Beekeeper and A Working Man . His survival thriller with Pitt turned out to be his third critical and commercial success in three years — a welcome return to form, considering the difficult phase Ayer endured after the Suicide Squad fiasco.

 Ten questions · five legends · one partner 
 Five legends. Five completely different ways of getting out alive: with style, with muscle, with charm, with luck, or with a plan so intricate it probably should not work. Ten questions will reveal which action hero was built to have your back.

 Question 01 of 10 THE MISSION 
 01 
 You are dropped into a dangerous situation with no warning. What do you need most from a partner? 
 The first few seconds tell you everything about who belongs beside you. 
 A Someone who already has three contingency plans running and is calmly working through all of them. 
 B Someone who reads the terrain by instinct and knows exactly how to use it against the enemy. 
 C Someone who keeps their nerve and their sense of humor while everything falls apart. 
 D Someone who knows the history of wherever we are and what we are walking into. 
 E Someone with the right contact, the right cover identity and the right exit already arranged.

 Question 02 of 10 TRAVEL STYLE 
 02 
 You have to get somewhere dangerous, fast. How do you travel? 
 How you get there is half the mission. 
 A On foot through terrain nobody else would attempt. I move where vehicles cannot follow. 
 B On a motorcycle, a cargo plane, or anything that gets me there before I think too hard about it. 
 C In something that belongs to someone else: borrowed, stolen, or improvised under fire. 
 D First class, with a cover identity and a gadget I will not explain until it is needed. 
 E By whatever is available. I have driven, flown, and once arrived by camel. The destination matters, not the method.

 Question 03 of 10 UNDER PRESSURE 
 03 
 You are cornered and outnumbered. What does your ideal partner do? 
 This is when you find out what somebody is really made of. 
 A Disappears into the environment, comes around behind them, and has it finished before I have moved. 
 B Cracks a one-liner, grabs a fire extinguisher or a chair, and improvises something that somehow works. 
 C Produces a gadget designed for this exact scenario and uses it with infuriating precision. 
 D Pulls out a whip, a bluff and an archaeological insight that somehow gets us out alive. 
 E Shuts it down with maximum efficiency and minimum words. They were already three moves ahead.

 Question 04 of 10 DOWNTIME 
 04 
 The mission is paused. You have one evening to decompress. What does your partner suggest? 
 Who somebody is when the pressure drops is who they really are. 
 A The finest restaurant in the city, a bottle of something expensive, and a conversation that is equal parts brilliant and exhausting. 
 B A local dig site, a museum after hours, or a long story about why that one artifact matters to human civilization. 
 C Pizza. Bad TV. Falling asleep halfway through a film neither of you was watching anyway. 
 D A bar with terrible lighting, cold beer, and absolutely no questions about feelings. 
 E A debrief that turns into three hours of contingency planning and somehow becomes the most fun you have had all week.

 Question 05 of 10 COMMUNICATION 
 05 
 How do you want your partner to communicate mid-mission? 
 Good communication is the difference between a partner and a liability. 
 A Precise and minimal. Tell me what I need and nothing else. Every word has a cost. 
 B Deadpan and dry. Keeping it light keeps me sharp, even when everything is on fire. 
 C Enthusiastic and slightly chaotic, but always with useful information buried in the noise. 
 D Calm and controlled through an earpiece, with a plan covering every variable I have not thought of yet. 
 E Barely at all. Silence is a language and they speak it fluently.

 Question 06 of 10 THE VILLAIN 
 06 
 Your enemy is powerful, well-resourced and holds the upper hand. How should your partner go at them? 
 The approach to the enemy defines the partnership. 
 A Infiltrate the inner circle, learn everything, and take them apart from inside before they know we are there. 
 B Study the historical pattern. Every villain of this type has a weakness written down somewhere in the past. 
 C Get them talking. The longer they monologue, the more time I have to work out how to beat them. 
 D Go straight at them, directly, using every inch of the terrain. 
 E Find the one thing they have not accounted for, because there is always one, and make sure we are holding it.

 Question 07 of 10 LOYALTY 
 07 
 It goes badly wrong and you are stranded somewhere hostile. What do you trust your partner to do? 
 Who somebody is when you need them most is the only thing that counts. 
 A Come in alone, quietly, and get me out before anybody knows they were there. 
 B Have been working the extraction since the moment I vanished. The plan is already running. 
 C Come in loud, come in fast, and worry about the collateral damage later. I would do the same for them. 
 D Use every resource, every contact, and bend every rule until I am out. They do not leave people behind. 
 E Charm their way in somehow, bluff through the hard part, and still manage to look good doing it.

 What does your ideal partner bring that you could not replace? 
 A great partner fills the gap you did not know you had. 
 A Technology that should not exist yet and the training to use it in any conditions. 
 B Survival instinct so refined it borders on supernatural, and the scars that prove it has been tested. 
 C Knowledge of history, language and culture that makes them priceless where force is useless. 
 D The ability to walk into any room on earth and immediately become the most trusted person in it. 
 E Stubbornness that will not accept a situation is hopeless, and the improvisation to back it up.

 Question 09 of 10 THE COST 
 09 
 Every partnership has a cost. Which of these can you live with? 
 Nobody comes without baggage. The question is whether you can carry it together. 
 A A partner who never fully switches off, always watching exits and counting threats, even at dinner. 
 B A partner who does the job brilliantly and has the emotional availability of a locked filing cabinet. 
 C A partner who makes everything ten times more complicated than it needs to be, and always comes through. 
 D A partner who gets personally attached to every relic and ruin we pass, which slows the whole thing down. 
 E A partner who was never built for this and knows it, but turns up anyway, every time, unasked.

 Question 10 of 10 THE LAST STAND 
 10 
 Final moment. Everything is on the line. What do you need from your partner right now? 
 The last question is the most honest one. 
 A One line. Absolutely dry. Delivered like the world is not ending. Then we move. 
 B Nothing said at all. Just a look that means you both already know what happens next. 
 C A plan I do not fully understand that somehow accounts for everything, laid out in thirty seconds. 
 D A piece of historical context that reframes the whole situation and says exactly what to do. 
 E Somebody who steps forward instead of back, because that is who they have always been.

 Olive channel locked 
 Rambo 
 The 1982 original 
 You will never need to ask whether he has your back. You will just know. 
 Your partner does not talk much, does not need to, and will have counted every threat around you before you finish your first sentence. John Rambo is not a man of plans or politics. He is a force shaped by survival, loyalty and an endurance that no amount of training produces on its own. He does not leave people behind. What you get is the most quietly ferocious partner imaginable, somebody who went through what would have broken anybody else and decided to keep going. 
 Why he is your partner 
 He reads ground the way other people read a room.
 He will stand between you and the worst of it without discussing it.
 He says almost nothing, and never the wrong thing.
 From the Collider file 
 The 1982 original came from David Morrell's 1972 novel, which ends very differently.
 Stallone cut most of his own dialogue in the edit to make the character nearly silent.
 Five films across thirty-seven years, from 1982 to the fifth in 2019.
 Says little 
 Leaves nobody 
 Built to endure 
 here -->
 Gold channel locked 
 James Bond 
 Dr. No, 1962 
 He has survived things that have no business being survivable, and he does it with style. 
 Your partner arrives perfectly dressed, perfectly briefed, and with a cover story convincing enough that you will need a moment to recall what is true. Bond is the most professionally dangerous person in any room he walks into and the most disarmingly charming, which is the whole point. He works in layers, where nothing is what it looks like and every advantage gets used without apology. You will never be bored. You will occasionally be furious. 
 Why he is your partner 
 He is better in the room than he is on paper, and he is excellent on paper.
 He will not explain the plan, and the plan will work.
 He treats charm as a tool, and it is a remarkably effective one.
 From the Collider file 
 Eon has made twenty-five Bond films since Dr. No in 1962, across six actors.
 Denis Villeneuve is directing the next one for Amazon MGM, which took creative control in
 2025.
 The search for the new 007 was still running through 2026, with screen tests under way.
 Charm as a tool 
 Always briefed 
 Unbothered 
 here -->
 Tan channel locked 
 Indiana Jones 
 Raiders of the Lost Ark, 1981 
 A scholar's eye and a brawler's instinct, which is an unusual pairing and a very effective one. 
 Your partner knows the history, the language, the cultural context, and exactly why the thing everyone else is ignoring is the most important object in the room. Indiana Jones is brilliant, reckless and occasionally impossible, and also one of the most genuinely resourceful people you could have beside you. He hates snakes and gets attached to objects of historical significance, both of which will slow you down at least once. It will not matter. 
 Why he is your partner 
 He has read the thing nobody else thought to read.
 He will risk the whole plan for the artifact, and be right about half the time.
 He improvises better than most people prepare.
 From the Collider file 
 The Cairo swordsman scene was improvised on the day because Harrison Ford had dysentery.
 Raiders was filmed in about 73 days, which was fast even in 1981.
 Dial of Destiny in 2023 was Ford's fifth and last outing, at the age of eighty.
 Knows the history 
 Reckless scholar 
 Improviser 
 here -->
 Red channel locked 
 John McClane 
 Die Hard, 1988 
 His superpower is stubbornness and his contingency plan is improvisation. 
 Your partner was not supposed to be here. He does not have the right equipment, the right information, or anything resembling the right odds. He has a sarcastic remark and a flat refusal to accept that the situation is as bad as it plainly is. John McClane is the great accidental hero of action cinema, a man whose capacity to absorb more than anybody should and keep going would be alarming if it were not so useful. He will complain the entire time. He will come through. 
 Why he is your partner 
 He turns whatever is in the room to his advantage.
 He is funniest when things are at their worst.
 He has never once agreed that it is over.
 From the Collider file 
 Die Hard came from Roderick Thorp's novel Nothing Lasts Forever, a sequel to a book
 filmed in 1968.
 Nakatomi Plaza is Fox Plaza, which was the studio's own headquarters at the time.
 Bruce Willis was a television comedy actor then, and a long way down the casting list.
 Pure stubbornness 
 Improvises 
 Complains throughout 
 here -->
 Blue channel locked 
 Ethan Hunt 
 Mission: Impossible, 1996 
 The mission will be impossible. He will complete it anyway. 
 Your partner has run seventeen scenarios before you finished the briefing, and the one he settled on involves at least two things that should not be physically possible. Ethan Hunt works at the outer edge of human capability, technically and physically, and he brings the same relentless precision to protecting his partners that he brings to dismantling organizations that should not exist. He is not easy to know and he will never tell you everything. He will carry the weight anyway. 
 Why he is your partner 
 He takes the risk himself rather than assigning it.
 He is three moves ahead and will not say which three.
 He treats your survival as the actual objective.
 From the Collider file 
 Cruise hung off the side of an Airbus A400M at a thousand feet for the opening of Rogue
 Nation.
 The HALO jump in Fallout took 106 takes, filmed at dusk for the light.
 The Final Reckoning in 2025 was the eighth film, and was sold as the last.
 Takes the risk 
 Never explains

 Here's When You Can Watch Brad Pitt's New Movie at Home
 The set of Fury was no cakewalk , and Pitt and Ayer reportedly butted heads over the final cut of their new movie as well. However, they arrived at common ground, and the movie emerged as a rollicking crowd-pleaser. We're talking, of course, about Heart of the Beast , which has so far grossed more than $180 million worldwide against a reported budget of $82 million. It remains to be seen if it has the legs to hit the $200 million mark, given that it has lost the majority of its theaters over the last few weeks.
 Heart of the Beast received excellent reviews and is now sitting at a "Certified Fresh" 84% score on the aggregator website Rotten Tomatoes. The site's consensus reads, "A rigorously entertaining adventure story told through a spartan script and memorable set pieces, Heart of the Beast pays rousing tribute to man's best friend." However, it's the film's "Verified Hot" 94% audience score that will serve it well in its PVOD run. The film lands on digital platforms on November 10, along with Jessica Chastain 's new horror film Other Mommy .
 Stay tuned to Collider for more updates.
